subject: general
question: 'Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment' as a Fundamental Right in the Indian Constitution is given in which Article of the Constitution ?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Article 16__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 16

 
 
• ​In regard to** public employment, equality of opportunity** is discussed in Article 16 of our constitution.
 
• **Article 16.1:-**
 
 
• The term "state" refers to the **central or state government**, state legislature, parliament, and all authorities and organizations governed by the Government of India.
 
• Every citizen of the nation will have** equal opportunities** whenever the state attempts to offer employment at a position controlled by "The state." Similar to how opportunities are the same for everyone, **laws are the same** for everyone.
 
 
 
• **Article 16.2:-**
 
 
• The government cannot discriminate against its citizens based on **religion, caste, birth, gender**, or descent when **offering employment** in state offices. Furthermore, none of the candidates will be disqualified based on these five criteria.
 
• Equal employment opportunity is the goal of both articles, but the Indian constitution only allows for the extension of articles 16.1 and 16.2 to offices controlled by "The State."
 
• This indicates that the state alone is obligated to adhere to article 16, not private organizations or employment with the state on a contract basis.
 
 
 
• **Article 16.3:-**
 
 
• Any **employment or appointment **in an office controlled by the state can be made subject to a residence requirement set by the **parliament**. Nobody can stop this.
 
• India has **22 official languages**, so it seems legitimate. Additionally, there are numerous** occupations **in which workers must interact with locals on a daily basis.
 
 
 
• **Article 16.4:-**
 
 
• Any **backward class** of citizens can have their **reservation** granted by the state. who, in the opinion of the state, are not adequately represented in the services provided by the state.
 
• Simply put, reservations can be granted by the government when **recruiting employees** for offices under their control. However, reservations can only be granted to members of the** lower class** and** not to members of the upper class** and the backward class must not be represented in government positions, and the government must do so.
 
 
 
• **Article 16.5:-**
 
 
• This indicates that the state can provide for the appointment of a person of the** same religion** to religious institutions.
 
• The fact that India is home to a **large number of different religions** lends credence to this provision.
 
• Additionally, each religion is** extremely sensitive** to its own** tradition.**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 14:-**

 
 
• **​**According to Article 14 of the Indian Constitution, all citizens are **treated equally under the law,** and it is against the law to discriminate based on gender, caste, religion, place of birth, or post.
 
• It is also a first **fundamental right** that talks about equality and demands that laws be made that allow for equal treatment.
 
 
 
• **Article 17:-**
 
 
• **​**It is against the law to practice **untouchability** in any form. Any disability that is enforced as a result of untouchability is illegal and subject to legal sanctions.
 
• From the perspective of equality before the law, Article 17 is also a significant provision (Article 14). It ensures **human dignity and social justice**, two rights that have been denied to a large portion of Indian society for centuries.
 
 
 
• **Article 15:-**
 
 
• **​**Any citizen shall not be subjected to **discrimination** on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth, or any combination thereof.
 
• Access to shops, public restaurants, hotels, and places of public entertainment **shall not be restricted or denied** to any citizen solely on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth, or any combination thereof; or the utilization of wells, tanks, bathing ghats, roads, and places of the public resort that are either entirely or partially funded by the **state **and made available to the general public.
